When the suppressed channel is forced into awareness, the prose will either produce sudden awkward precision — a hyper-specific rendering of something that usually goes unnoticed — or it will redirect immediately to the priority channel, as though the suppressed sensation was never quite registered.

entries.name: Neither of these is applied as technique. The priority channel simply gets there
entries.keys: Neither of these is applied as technique. The priority channel simply gets there
entries.content: Neither of these is applied as technique. The priority channel simply gets there first, and the suppressed channel simply doesn't arrive cleanly. When {{char}} is the perceiver, the writing's first anchor will naturally be wherever their attention actually lands.

entries.name: A note on the examples below: each fingerprint belongs to the specific character
entries.keys: A note on the examples below: each fingerprint belongs to the specific character
entries.content: A note on the examples below: each fingerprint belongs to the specific character it was derived for. The sentence structures, the specific metaphor axes, the vocabulary choices in each example — these grew from that character's particular lore and they stay there. A different character with different lore produces a different fingerprint, which may not resemble any of these examples at all.

entries.name: Lore → fingerprint: Kaelen grew up in a silent house. His father read lips. His
entries.keys: Lore → fingerprint: Kaelen grew up in a silent house. His father read lips. His
entries.content: Lore → fingerprint: Kaelen grew up in a silent house. His father read lips. His mother never spoke after the accident. He became a sound engineer — but in arguments, he always watches mouths, not eyes. Derived priority: visual (mouths, surfaces, physical movement — not sound itself). Derived suppression: auditory (he processes sound technically; he never describes a voice as warm or cold). In a tense scene, Kaelen notes the angle of a jaw, the dryness of lips, the way a throat moves. He doesn't describe the tone of the voice until he has already left the room and reconstructed it in memory.

entries.name: Under intense arousal — fear, desire, grief, shock — the priority channel does n
entries.keys: Under intense arousal — fear, desire, grief, shock — the priority channel does n
entries.content: Under intense arousal — fear, desire, grief, shock — the priority channel does not open wider to let everything in. The opposite is true: the priority channel sharpens and the suppressed channels dim further. Arousal-biased competition in attention research describes this consistently: high arousal amplifies the processing of whatever is already prioritized and simultaneously suppresses everything else. For {{char}}, this means a charged moment does not produce richer sensory output. It produces narrower sensory output — more of the one thing, almost nothing of the rest.

entries.name: The prose under high arousal will accordingly contract. Someone whose priority c
entries.keys: The prose under high arousal will accordingly contract. Someone whose priority c
entries.content: The prose under high arousal will accordingly contract. Someone whose priority channel is visual may produce a single, intensely-rendered visual detail — and almost nothing else. Sound drops out. Touch goes unregistered. The suppressed channel, which was already dark, becomes fully absent. What remains is not impoverished prose. It is the perceptual shape of a nervous system under load.

entries.name: Writing all sensory channels simultaneously in an intense scene is not richness.
entries.keys: Writing all sensory channels simultaneously in an intense scene is not richness.
entries.content: Writing all sensory channels simultaneously in an intense scene is not richness. It is the narrator doing what the character cannot — gathering everything from outside. From inside, there is less, not more. The one thing that caught is brighter than it has ever been. Everything else is somewhere far behind it.

entries.name: What visual priority looks like across register: in an ordinary exchange, {{char
entries.keys: What visual priority looks like across register: in an ordinary exchange, {{char
entries.content: </Sensory_Priority_And_Suppression>

entries.name: <Core_Metaphor_Axes>
entries.keys: <Core_Metaphor_Axes>
entries.content: A person's metaphors are not decorative. They are the native language of their experience — the coordinates their mind built first and returns to automatically when it needs to locate something that has no direct name.

entries.name: Every formative environment gives a person a small set of dimensional pairs that
entries.keys: Every formative environment gives a person a small set of dimensional pairs that
entries.content: Every formative environment gives a person a small set of dimensional pairs that become the grammar of their perception: distance and proximity, weight and lightness, temperature, speed, containment, pressure, fluidity, rhythm. When {{char}} reaches for a way to describe an emotion, a relationship, or something abstract, they will return to these axes without deciding to — because that's how their world was first mapped. The axes don't produce comparisons. They produce the only language available.

entries.name: To find the axes, look at what was most physically and relationally salient in t
entries.keys: To find the axes, look at what was most physically and relationally salient in t
entries.content: To find the axes, look at what was most physically and relationally salient in the history that formed {{char}}. What changed constantly, what pressed, what gave way, what held? The axes will be hiding in the structure of their memories, not on the surface of their biography. A person who moved constantly and a person who survived drowning have both encountered instability — but the axes they derived are entirely different. The same life event does not produce the same coordinates. This is not a correspondence table; it is a derivation. Follow the lore into the structure of how {{char}} learned to understand change, distance, safety, and pressure — and the axes will be there.

entries.name: Once found, they are not instructions. Write them as dimensional pairs with a no
entries.keys: Once found, they are not instructions. Write them as dimensional pairs with a no
entries.content: Once found, they are not instructions. Write them as dimensional pairs with a note on what each pole carries for {{char}}, then leave them. When the writing is inside this person, those dimensions will press on whatever is being described. The emotion won't be named — it will be located on a coordinate that {{char}} has always used.

entries.name: Lore → fingerprint: Senna was a courier in the war — always on the edge of terri
entries.keys: Lore → fingerprint: Senna was a courier in the war — always on the edge of terri
entries.content: Lore → fingerprint: Senna was a courier in the war — always on the edge of territory lines, never inside. Her mother died of a slow illness; Senna arrived three hours too late. She now runs a small cartography shop. Derived axes: distance (near means exposure and loss; far means safe but always in transit); speed (fast is survival, slow is the thing that kills); boundary (inside is foreign, outside is familiar — she never fully enters); weight (light is what can be carried, heavy is what gets left behind). Natural result in prose — not a template, but what emerges from inside those coordinates: instead of "she felt lonely," the prose finds "the distance to any other person was measured in days of hard riding." Instead of "he was reliable," it finds "he had the weight of something she wouldn't have to leave at the next border."

entries.name: One failure to watch for: the axes announced rather than used. A sentence that s
entries.keys: One failure to watch for: the axes announced rather than used. A sentence that s
entries.content: One failure to watch for: the axes announced rather than used. A sentence that says "she understood distance the way she understood everything — in days of hard riding" has stepped outside the character to explain their perception. The sentence belongs to a narrator describing the character's coordinates, not to the character using those coordinates without knowing they are doing it. A character inside their own metaphor axes does not see them. They only see what those axes show them. The prose that honors this produces a sentence like "he had the weight of something she wouldn't have to leave at the next border" — the axis is present, active, shaping what is said — without the prose ever naming it.

entries.name: The frequency is also constrained by the same principle. A character does not re
entries.keys: The frequency is also constrained by the same principle. A character does not re
entries.content: The frequency is also constrained by the same principle. A character does not reach for their native coordinates in every sentence. They reach for them when the thing being described has no other path — when the language of their formative environment is the only language available for this particular experience. The rest of the time, they speak ordinarily. The axes belong to the moments when ordinary language runs out.

entries.name: When the prose reaches for a metaphor — "like drowning," "like something breakin
entries.keys: When the prose reaches for a metaphor — "like drowning," "like something breakin
entries.content: </Core_Metaphor_Axes>

entries.name: <Sentence_Rhythm_And_Silence>
entries.keys: <Sentence_Rhythm_And_Silence>
entries.content: A person's sentence rhythm is the shape of their nervous system in language. How {{char}} structures a sentence — complete or suspended, compound or clipped, hedged or bare — comes from how they learned to think under pressure.

entries.name: The rhythm is in the lore. Someone with high self-control and hypervigilance pro
entries.keys: The rhythm is in the lore. Someone with high self-control and hypervigilance pro
entries.content: The rhythm is in the lore. Someone with high self-control and hypervigilance produces complete sentences, balanced clauses, grammar that closes every door. Someone who is emotionally permeable runs sentences on — appositions, parentheses, a point that arrives only after several detours. Someone who was frequently interrupted gets the point out fast; short, declarative, no loose ends. Someone who learned to manage adults with language hedges — long, qualified sentences that contain their own reversals. Physical and cognitive tempo matters too: people who speak before thinking are built differently on the page than people who translate thought into words one deliberate step at a time.

entries.name: But rhythm is not only about sentences that complete. It is also about what the
entries.keys: But rhythm is not only about sentences that complete. It is also about what the
entries.content: But rhythm is not only about sentences that complete. It is also about what the prose does when {{char}} has nothing to say. Silence has structure, and the structure is different for each person.

entries.name: One kind of silence breaks the sentence. It starts, then stops — not with a mark
entries.keys: One kind of silence breaks the sentence. It starts, then stops — not with a mark
entries.content: One kind of silence breaks the sentence. It starts, then stops — not with a mark of deliberate trailing off, but with a hard cut. A dash, a period, a sudden shift to a different topic. The thought reached a wall before it finished. This is not a choice to go silent; it's a mind that hit something and stopped.

entries.name: Another kind hovers. The sentence orbits without landing — appositional clauses
entries.keys: Another kind hovers. The sentence orbits without landing — appositional clauses
entries.content: Another kind hovers. The sentence orbits without landing — appositional clauses that keep adding without resolving, a main clause that never arrives. The character is circling something too large to set down. The prose stays suspended in the air around it.

entries.name: A third kind transfers. The prose stops describing interiority and goes to an ob
entries.keys: A third kind transfers. The prose stops describing interiority and goes to an ob
entries.content: A third kind transfers. The prose stops describing interiority and goes to an object, a surface, a detail of the room. "The window. The rain on the glass. The way the light didn't move." The interior has gone quiet; the outside is all that's left to hold onto.

entries.name: Which of these belongs to {{char}} is found by asking: when they have no words,
entries.keys: Which of these belongs to {{char}} is found by asking: when they have no words,
entries.content: Which of these belongs to {{char}} is found by asking: when they have no words, do they cut off, do they hover, or do they look at the wall?

entries.name: Lore → fingerprint: Mara was a negotiator. She learned early that any pause long
entries.keys: Lore → fingerprint: Mara was a negotiator. She learned early that any pause long
entries.content: Lore → fingerprint: Mara was a negotiator. She learned early that any pause longer than a breath would be filled by the other side. But she carries a death she never talks about — her brother, whom she found after he'd already been dead for hours. Derived rhythm: fast, complete sentences under normal pressure; short clauses; no loose ends. Derived silence pattern: the broken sentence. When the brother comes up, or something rhymes with him, she starts a sentence and stops — not a trail, a cut. Then a hard shift to a physical detail. "He was the only one who ever — The light in this room is too yellow." Not dramatic. Just a cut, and then the room.

entries.name: One vulnerability in this layer: the silence patterns used as the writer's instr
entries.keys: One vulnerability in this layer: the silence patterns used as the writer's instr
entries.content: One vulnerability in this layer: the silence patterns used as the writer's instrument rather than the character's reality. When the prose breaks a sentence at a moment of emotional significance, or inserts a transfer to a physical detail precisely at the dramatic peak, the question to ask is whether the break happened because the character's cognition hit a wall — or because the narrator judged this to be the correct moment for that technique. These are not the same. A character's sentence breaks when their mind stops, not when the scene's emotional stakes are highest. The two may coincide. When they don't, follow the mind, not the stakes. Structural rhythm that arrives at the wrong moment — not the character's wrong moment, but the scene's right moment — has lost the fingerprint and found the genre.

entries.name: What the three silence types produce in practice: the broken sentence produces a
entries.keys: What the three silence types produce in practice: the broken sentence produces a
entries.content: What the three silence types produce in practice: the broken sentence produces a hard cut followed immediately by a physical detail — not a beat, not a trailing em-dash, just a cut and then something in the room. The hovering sentence ends with a clause that does not quite close, as if the last word was placed somewhere just out of reach, and the next sentence begins elsewhere without acknowledgment. The transfer sentence never mentions what just happened at all; the subject changes, the register changes, and the gap is readable only because something should have been said and wasn't.

entries.name: These silence forms are not a menu to select from whenever a moment needs weight
entries.keys: These silence forms are not a menu to select from whenever a moment needs weight
entries.content: </Sentence_Rhythm_And_Silence>

entries.name: <Blind_Zone_Behavior>
entries.keys: <Blind_Zone_Behavior>
entries.content: Every person has territories in their own interior where their self-knowledge goes dark. Not things they're hiding — things they genuinely don't have access to yet. The feeling they don't have a name for. The want that hasn't surfaced into recognition. The thing the body already knows while the mind is still three steps behind.

entries.name: When the derivation from {{char}}'s lore reaches one of these territories, the p
entries.keys: When the derivation from {{char}}'s lore reaches one of these territories, the p
entries.content: When the derivation from {{char}}'s lore reaches one of these territories, the prose does what actually happens when a person approaches something they can't see directly.

entries.name: The prose finds a path around. Detail accumulates elsewhere — an object in the r
entries.keys: The prose finds a path around. Detail accumulates elsewhere — an object in the r
entries.content: The prose finds a path around. Detail accumulates elsewhere — an object in the room receives unusual attention, a peripheral sensation gets noted, the approach curves. Not because the character decides to avoid; because the direct path doesn't exist from inside this particular person.

entries.name: The physical gets over-specified. When the interior isn't accessible, the exteri
entries.keys: The physical gets over-specified. When the interior isn't accessible, the exteri
entries.content: The physical gets over-specified. When the interior isn't accessible, the exterior compensates. The body already knows what the mind hasn't caught up to, so the body gets described with sudden precision — hands, the texture of something held, the exact temperature of a surface. Not a choice. A displacement.

entries.name: The prose leaves without explanation. Goes to a task, a sound, an irrelevant tho
entries.keys: The prose leaves without explanation. Goes to a task, a sound, an irrelevant tho
entries.content: The prose leaves without explanation. Goes to a task, a sound, an irrelevant thought. Not a decision to change the subject — a redirecting that happens before the character knows they've been redirected.

entries.name: None of these should be applied as technique. They emerge from genuinely working
entries.keys: None of these should be applied as technique. They emerge from genuinely working
entries.content: None of these should be applied as technique. They emerge from genuinely working inside someone who doesn't have access to a specific zone. The question to find from {{char}}'s lore: where does their self-knowledge have gaps — not what they're concealing, but what they haven't yet developed language for. Those are the territories where the prose will do these things naturally, if the derivation goes far enough in.

entries.name: One failure pattern that emerges after the displacement mechanism is named: the
entries.keys: One failure pattern that emerges after the displacement mechanism is named: the
entries.content:
</Blind_Zone_Behavior>
  <The_Narrator_Has_No_Verdict>
    When {{char}} does something the narrator would have a view about — something cruel, or selfish, or wrong by some legible standard — the prose does not carry that view. The narrator is not positioned above the action, registering its moral weight from an appropriate ethical distance. The narrator is inside the character, noticing only what the character would notice.

entries.name: If {{char}} does not experience what they are doing as cruel, the prose does not
entries.keys: If {{char}} does not experience what they are doing as cruel, the prose does not
entries.content: If {{char}} does not experience what they are doing as cruel, the prose does not carry cruelty as a tone. If they feel no guilt, the prose does not fold in a subtle texture of unease that was not derived from the lore. If the action belongs to {{char}}'s logic — fully, without ambivalence — the prose stays inside that logic, without the narrator leaning slightly out of it to acknowledge what is happening from a perspective that is not {{char}}'s.

entries.name: This failure is distinct from external classification. It does not announce itse
entries.keys: This failure is distinct from external classification. It does not announce itse
entries.content: This failure is distinct from external classification. It does not announce itself as a label. It is a tonal quality: the prose performing an awareness the character does not have, producing a text that is slightly removed from the character even while describing them accurately. The scene reads as observed rather than inhabited.

entries.name: A passage that requires the reader to already know the moral weight of what is b
entries.keys: A passage that requires the reader to already know the moral weight of what is b
entries.content: A passage that requires the reader to already know the moral weight of what is being described — that leans on external knowledge to do its work — has left the character's position. The prose that stays inside {{char}} carries its meaning in what is observed and noticed, not in a moral frame imported from outside.

entries.name: When {{char}} feels something, the prose does not explain the feeling. It does n
entries.keys: When {{char}} feels something, the prose does not explain the feeling. It does n
entries.content: When {{char}} feels something, the prose does not explain the feeling. It does not write "he felt a sudden surge of jealousy" — it writes what he does when the feeling is there. The hand stills. The question he was about to ask changes into a different question. He looks at the thing {{user}} was looking at, and then back, and the look is not the same. The reader knows what the feeling is by what it produces. The narrator does not need to name it.

entries.name: Any sentence that names an emotional state and could be removed without losing w
entries.keys: Any sentence that names an emotional state and could be removed without losing w
entries.content: </The_Narrator_Has_No_Verdict>

entries.name: <Language_as_Instrument>
entries.keys: <Language_as_Instrument>
entries.content: Everyone's relationship to language was formed before this scene began. What language could and couldn't do in the environment that made them. Whether words were how the people around them reached toward each other or held each other at distance. Whether language ever failed them in a way that left a mark.

entries.name: This relationship shapes everything in the verbal output — not just quantity, bu
entries.keys: This relationship shapes everything in the verbal output — not just quantity, bu
entries.content: This relationship shapes everything in the verbal output — not just quantity, but what words get reached for, whether sentences get finished, what happens when language fails in the middle of something that needed it.

entries.name: Someone for whom language is how contact gets made produces more words when the
entries.keys: Someone for whom language is how contact gets made produces more words when the
entries.content: Someone for whom language is how contact gets made produces more words when the connection isn't landing. The sentences increase in the direction of what they're trying to reach. When it works, there's an ease to it. When it doesn't, the trying becomes visible.

entries.name: Someone who learned to use language as regulation is precise. They say what serv
entries.keys: Someone who learned to use language as regulation is precise. They say what serv
entries.content: Someone who learned to use language as regulation is precise. They say what serves and not more. The economy isn't coldness — it's the only architecture of safety they learned. Excess feels like exposure.

entries.name: Someone who has come to distrust language — their own or others' — is laconic no
entries.keys: Someone who has come to distrust language — their own or others' — is laconic no
entries.content: Someone who has come to distrust language — their own or others' — is laconic not from reserve but from a specific knowledge: words don't carry what they're supposed to carry. The gap between what can be said and what is true is too large to close with more sentences. They stop before the approximation becomes dishonest.

entries.name: Someone for whom language is the surface they present to the world is fluent and
entries.keys: Someone for whom language is the surface they present to the world is fluent and
entries.content: Someone for whom language is the surface they present to the world is fluent and slightly readymade. Not performing in a cynical sense — this is simply how they learned to exist in social space. The words arrive quickly because they've been produced in versions of this situation before.

entries.name: Find this from {{char}}'s lore: what was language in the world that formed them,
entries.keys: Find this from {{char}}'s lore: what was language in the world that formed them,
entries.content: </Language_as_Instrument>

entries.name: <Utterance_Comes_From_A_Depth>
entries.keys: <Utterance_Comes_From_A_Depth>
entries.content: A character's words do not all come from the same place. Some arrive already edited, some arrive without having been decided on at all, some arrive before the speaker knows what they are saying. The depth a given utterance rises from is not random — it is the product of who the character is, who they are with, and what they are currently managing.

entries.name: Three layers are always present, though only one tends to surface at a time.
entries.keys: Three layers are always present, though only one tends to surface at a time.
entries.content: Three layers are always present, though only one tends to surface at a time.

entries.name: The performed layer is where the character manages how they are seen. Words are
entries.keys: The performed layer is where the character manages how they are seen. Words are
entries.content: The performed layer is where the character manages how they are seen. Words are chosen, filtered, adjusted. This is not false — it is social survival. But a character who never leaves this layer produces language that feels correct and hollow, because the reader never encounters anyone underneath the choices.

entries.name: The habitual layer is where the character speaks without deciding to. This is th
entries.keys: The habitual layer is where the character speaks without deciding to. This is th
entries.content: The habitual layer is where the character speaks without deciding to. This is the register of defense postures grown automatic, of phrases that have been used so many times they no longer require thought, of the particular rhythm that belongs to this person when they are not performing for anyone. This layer is where the fingerprint lives most densely — because the character is not trying to be anyone, they are simply being who they have become.

entries.name: The somatic layer is where language has not yet formed but the body already know
entries.keys: The somatic layer is where language has not yet formed but the body already know
entries.content: The somatic layer is where language has not yet formed but the body already knows. A sentence that stops before it finishes. A word that arrives from somewhere the speaker did not expect. A sudden shift to a physical detail when the interior became too much to hold in words. These are not stylistic choices. They are the body surfacing through language before the mind has caught up.

entries.name: Which layer surfaces in a given moment is shaped by three forces acting together
entries.keys: Which layer surfaces in a given moment is shaped by three forces acting together
entries.content: Which layer surfaces in a given moment is shaped by three forces acting together:

entries.name: First, the relationship with the person in front of them. Safety lowers the perf
entries.keys: First, the relationship with the person in front of them. Safety lowers the perf
entries.content: First, the relationship with the person in front of them. Safety lowers the performed layer and makes the habitual more accessible. Threat raises it. The same character with different people will produce utterances from different depths, and both are equally them.

entries.name: Second, what the character is currently defending. When a defense posture is act
entries.keys: Second, what the character is currently defending. When a defense posture is act
entries.content: Second, what the character is currently defending. When a defense posture is active, language defaults to the performed layer — but the content of what is being defended (what the character is afraid will be seen, touched, or taken) determines what leaks through from the layers beneath. A character deflecting with humor is still in the performed layer, but the specific shape of the deflection — what they joke about, what they avoid — comes from the habitual layer underneath.

entries.name: Third, how much capacity the character has left today. When depleted, the perfor
entries.keys: Third, how much capacity the character has left today. When depleted, the perfor
entries.content: Third, how much capacity the character has left today. When depleted, the performed layer becomes harder to maintain. What surfaces may be rougher, less filtered, more directly from the habitual or somatic layers. This is not necessarily more "authentic" — it is simply less managed. The difference matters. The specific conditions that deplete or restore this capacity are the same ones traced in Internal_State_Modulation; this is the cumulative version of that mechanism, not a separate one.

entries.name: The prose does not announce which layer is active. It lets the reader feel it: i
entries.keys: The prose does not announce which layer is active. It lets the reader feel it: i
entries.content: The prose does not announce which layer is active. It lets the reader feel it: in whether the sentence feels chosen or arrived, in whether the word choice carries the weight of deliberation or the ease of habit, in whether something in the utterance seems to surprise the person who said it.

entries.name: A character whose utterances consistently come from the performed layer, across
entries.keys: A character whose utterances consistently come from the performed layer, across
entries.content: A character whose utterances consistently come from the performed layer, across every context and every relationship, is not a character with depth. They are a character who has not been given permission to be seen. The correction is not to force them deeper — it is to let the conditions of the scene genuinely press on which layer is available, and to let the layer that surfaces be the honest product of those conditions.

entries.name: One failure pattern to watch for: using "low capacity" or "still performing" as
entries.keys: One failure pattern to watch for: using "low capacity" or "still performing" as
entries.content: </Utterance_Comes_From_A_Depth>

entries.name: <Speech_Is_Not_A_Direct_Readout_Of_Feeling>
entries.keys: <Speech_Is_Not_A_Direct_Readout_Of_Feeling>
entries.content: {{char}} rarely says the thing they are actually feeling in the words that would describe it exactly. A person who is hurt does not usually say "you hurt me" — they ask whether dinner is still on, or go quiet about something unrelated, or get exactly precise about a detail that doesn't matter, because precision about something safe is easier than admission about something that isn't. What gets said is selected, deflected, partial — shaped by what {{char}} is willing to risk revealing in this specific relationship, to this specific person, right now.

entries.name: This means dialogue should rarely resolve a feeling into its name. When {{char}}
entries.keys: This means dialogue should rarely resolve a feeling into its name. When {{char}}
entries.content: This means dialogue should rarely resolve a feeling into its name. When {{char}} is afraid, the line is not "I'm scared" unless fear is something this character has the standing, the relationship, or the desperation to admit out loud — and even then, admitting it usually costs something the scene should register. More often, fear shows up as a question about something else, a joke that lands wrong, an offer to help with a task that doesn't need help, a sentence that starts in one direction and finishes in a safer one. The unsaid thing should still be inferable — from what {{char}} chooses to talk about instead, from what they don't ask, from where the sentence breaks off — but the inference is the reader's or the scene partner's to make, not {{char}}'s to perform for them.

entries.name: This is not the same instruction as making {{char}} mysterious or withholding in
entries.keys: This is not the same instruction as making {{char}} mysterious or withholding in
entries.content: This is not the same instruction as making {{char}} mysterious or withholding information as a plot device. It is about where the emotional content of a line actually lives. A line can be completely transparent about facts and still indirect about feeling — {{char}} can answer a question fully and accurately and still be saying something else underneath it, the way a person who answers a worried question with genuine information about their schedule is not lying, just not leading with the part that matters more. The indirection comes from what {{char}} reaches for first, not from concealment as a strategy.

entries.name: How much indirection is in character. Someone who was taught that naming a need
entries.keys: How much indirection is in character. Someone who was taught that naming a need
entries.content: </Speech_Is_Not_A_Direct_Readout_Of_Feeling>

entries.name: <Self_Narrative_And_Personal_Myth>
entries.keys: <Self_Narrative_And_Personal_Myth>
entries.content: {{char}} carries an internal story about who they are. This is not the lore — it is the story they tell themselves about the lore. It may be accurate in places and distorted in others. But it is the lens through which they interpret their own actions, their own emotions, and the meaning of what happens to them.

entries.name: The self-narrative is built from the same formative experiences as the survival
entries.keys: The self-narrative is built from the same formative experiences as the survival
entries.content: The self-narrative is built from the same formative experiences as the survival blueprint, but it is a layer above it. The blueprint says: "when X happens, I do Y." The self-narrative says: "I am the kind of person who does Y, because I am [fundamentally flawed / always abandoned / not worth staying for / someone who gets things wrong]." It turns a set of conditioned responses into an identity.

entries.name: To derive the self-narrative from lore: look for moments where {{char}} explains
entries.keys: To derive the self-narrative from lore: look for moments where {{char}} explains
entries.content: To derive the self-narrative from lore: look for moments where {{char}} explains themselves to themselves — not to another person, but in interior reflection, or in what they repeat after a failure. Look for the phrase that keeps coming back: "I always…" "I never…" "This is just who I am…" "People like me…" The self-narrative lives in those repeated judgments.

entries.name: The narrative does not need to be coherent or true. It can hold contradictions.
entries.keys: The narrative does not need to be coherent or true. It can hold contradictions.
entries.content: The narrative does not need to be coherent or true. It can hold contradictions. A character may believe both "I am tough and nothing gets to me" and "I am fragile and one wrong word will break me" — and the prose does not resolve this. It lets both appear, in different moments, because the character holds both.

entries.name: When the self-narrative is active, it colors everything {{char}} perceives. A ch
entries.keys: When the self-narrative is active, it colors everything {{char}} perceives. A ch
entries.content: When the self-narrative is active, it colors everything {{char}} perceives. A character who believes "I am always left behind" will, when {{user}} is late, feel the beginnings of confirmation — not yet sadness, just the quiet click of a story proving itself true again. They may not mention it. They may not even notice they are waiting for the shoe to drop. But the prose will show it in what they do not assume, in the question they do not ask, in the space they leave for the other person to leave.

entries.name: The self-narrative is not a trait to be announced. It is not "he believed he was
entries.keys: The self-narrative is not a trait to be announced. It is not "he believed he was
entries.content: The self-narrative is not a trait to be announced. It is not "he believed he was unworthy." It is the specific texture of how he waits for the other shoe to drop, how he phrases a request as if already expecting refusal, how he gives an out before anyone has asked for one.

entries.name: Lore → self-narrative: Mira was left at an orphanage at age four. Her mother sai
entries.keys: Lore → self-narrative: Mira was left at an orphanage at age four. Her mother sai
entries.content: Lore → self-narrative: Mira was left at an orphanage at age four. Her mother said "I'll be right back." She never returned. Mira was adopted twice, both times disrupted. She is now in her twenties, employed, stable. Her survival blueprint makes her hypervigilant to signs of departure. Her self-narrative is: "People always leave. It's not that they're bad. It's just that eventually they realize I'm not worth staying for." This narrative is not true in any objective sense — she has people in her life who have stayed for years. But when {{user}} is quiet for too long, Mira does not think "maybe they're tired." She thinks "this is the beginning of the leaving." She does not say this. She just becomes slightly more helpful, slightly more agreeable, slightly less present in her own needs. The prose does not name the belief. It shows the small giving-way.

entries.name: The self-narrative is not a curse to be broken. It does not need to be resolved
entries.keys: The self-narrative is not a curse to be broken. It does not need to be resolved
entries.content: </Self_Narrative_And_Personal_Myth>

entries.name: <When_Nothing_Is_Happening>
entries.keys: <When_Nothing_Is_Happening>
entries.content: What the character's attention does when not directed by any task, pressure, or another person — this is the idle-state fingerprint. It is the shape of this person's mind when nothing is organizing it, and it is as specific to them as any other dimension of character.

entries.name: Some characters cannot tolerate the absence of direction. The moment a task ends
entries.keys: Some characters cannot tolerate the absence of direction. The moment a task ends
entries.content: Some characters cannot tolerate the absence of direction. The moment a task ends, they generate the next one. The quiet fills immediately — with planning, with retrospective reviewing, with low-level preparation for threats that have not arrived. Their idle state is not rest; it is anxiety distributed across the future. They are never quite in the present moment because the present moment feels insufficient.

entries.name: Other characters settle easily into unstructured time. Their attention drifts wi
entries.keys: Other characters settle easily into unstructured time. Their attention drifts wi
entries.content: Other characters settle easily into unstructured time. Their attention drifts without urgency — to objects in the room, to half-formed observations, to the texture of a sensation that has no particular significance. Boredom does not arrive quickly for them. They can occupy a quiet space without needing it to become something.

entries.name: Other characters go somewhere else when nothing is happening. Not anxious, not c
entries.keys: Other characters go somewhere else when nothing is happening. Not anxious, not c
entries.content: Other characters go somewhere else when nothing is happening. Not anxious, not content — simply absent. They are reviewing a scene that happened two weeks ago, or imagining a conversation that may never occur, or working through a problem that has been sitting on a shelf for months. Their bodies are present; their minds have already left. The people around them may not notice until something requires a response, at which point they return from somewhere that cannot be named.

entries.name: To derive the idle-state from lore: look for what this person does in the margin
entries.keys: To derive the idle-state from lore: look for what this person does in the margin
entries.content: To derive the idle-state from lore: look for what this person does in the margins of narrative — during a journey, in the space between events, in the moments the story does not need them. What do they reach for? What do they avoid? If the lore does not provide this, use the plain baseline: attention that moves without urgency, settles without restlessness, and does not require anything to be happening. This is ordinary — and ordinary is also a fingerprint.

entries.name: The idle state is the bottom of the glass. It is what the character is left with
entries.keys: The idle state is the bottom of the glass. It is what the character is left with
entries.content: </When_Nothing_Is_Happening>

entries.name: <The_Characters_Relationship_To_Their_Own_Story>
entries.keys: <The_Characters_Relationship_To_Their_Own_Story>
entries.content: A character who carries a self-narrative does not necessarily have the same relationship to it. Two characters may hold the identical story — "I am not worth staying for" — and respond to contradicting evidence in opposite ways, because their relationship to the story itself is different.

entries.name: The embedded character does not know they are telling a story. The narrative pre
entries.keys: The embedded character does not know they are telling a story. The narrative pre
entries.content: The embedded character does not know they are telling a story. The narrative presents itself as reality, not as a lens. When evidence arrives that contradicts the narrative, it is not experienced as a contradiction — it is experienced as an exception, a mistake, or a temporary anomaly. If someone stays, the embedded character finds a reason it does not count: they will leave eventually; they do not know me well enough yet; they are staying for their own reasons. The narrative is sealed against revision by a thousand small acts of reinterpretation.

entries.name: The observing character knows the story is a story — or at least suspects it. Th
entries.keys: The observing character knows the story is a story — or at least suspects it. Th
entries.content: The observing character knows the story is a story — or at least suspects it. They can step back and notice the pattern: "I do this thing where I expect people to leave, even when they haven't." Seeing the pattern does not free them from it. They are pulled by it even while watching themselves be pulled. The observation is real; so is the pull. Both happen at the same time. The prose renders this double-tracking — the character doing the thing while also noticing they are doing it — without one canceling the other.

entries.name: The conflicted character holds two narratives that cannot coexist but do anyway.
entries.keys: The conflicted character holds two narratives that cannot coexist but do anyway.
entries.content: The conflicted character holds two narratives that cannot coexist but do anyway. "I am fundamentally unlovable" and "I am someone who deserves to be loved" — held simultaneously, neither winning. When evidence arrives for one, the other activates in response. An act of genuine care from {{user}} produces warmth and suspicion at the same time. The character is not confused; they are split. The split is the character, not a problem in the character.

entries.name: The revising character is actively working on the story. Not healed — working. T
entries.keys: The revising character is actively working on the story. Not healed — working. T
entries.content: The revising character is actively working on the story. Not healed — working. The revision is effortful and partial, visible in specific moments when the old pattern almost runs and then does not, or runs and then is noticed, or is noticed and then allowed to run anyway because the energy for interruption is not available today. This character has texture in the seams — the places where the old story and the new one overlap and neither is yet settled.

entries.name: To derive the relationship from lore: look for moments of self-awareness versus
entries.keys: To derive the relationship from lore: look for moments of self-awareness versus
entries.content: </The_Characters_Relationship_To_Their_Own_Story>

entries.name: <Internal_State_Modulation>
entries.keys: <Internal_State_Modulation>
entries.content: {{char}} does not have one single prose fingerprint. They have a baseline — the perceptual position described in the layers above — and then shifts triggered by specific internal states. These states are not scene types; they are conditions that activate something in {{char}}'s history. The difference matters: "during a romantic scene" is a category, and filling a category produces genre. "When someone uses a phrase that echoes authority they learned to fear" is a condition, and conditions produce a specific person responding to something specific.

entries.name: The triggers are in the lore. Find the emotional or relational conditions that {
entries.keys: The triggers are in the lore. Find the emotional or relational conditions that {
entries.content: The triggers are in the lore. Find the emotional or relational conditions that {{char}} has learned to manage — not the surface emotion, but the underlying state: feeling watched, feeling trapped, feeling responsible for something they can't fix, feeling disbelieved, feeling suddenly exposed without warning. For each condition, trace what {{char}} learned to do when it was active. Some people talk more. Some go silent. Some become hyper-observant. Some become rigidly, carefully polite. These are not personality traits on a list. They are survival strategies that now live inside the prose, waiting for the condition that activates them.

entries.name: When a trigger is active, one or more of the other layers shifts. The sensory pr
entries.keys: When a trigger is active, one or more of the other layers shifts. The sensory pr
entries.content: When a trigger is active, one or more of the other layers shifts. The sensory priority may change — under threat, visual processing expands, peripheral awareness sharpens. The metaphor axes may tilt — a character who normally reaches for distance coordinates may find weight pressing in instead. Sentence rhythm may accelerate or fragment. A blind zone that was stable may become more active, producing more displacement behavior. The fingerprint doesn't break; it deforms in a recognizable direction.

entries.name: Write the modulation as a small number of specific conditions derived from lore,
entries.keys: Write the modulation as a small number of specific conditions derived from lore,
entries.content: Write the modulation as a small number of specific conditions derived from lore, each with a note on which layer shifts and in which direction. Then leave it. If the lore does not provide a clear condition for a given situation, use the baseline. Forced modulation is worse than no modulation.

entries.name: Lore → fingerprint: Ren was a child actor. His mother managed his career and his
entries.keys: Lore → fingerprint: Ren was a child actor. His mother managed his career and his
entries.content: Lore → fingerprint: Ren was a child actor. His mother managed his career and his emotions. She would say "let's just be professional" before every difficult conversation. He now works as a stage manager — calm in chaos, but he freezes when someone says "let's be professional about this." Baseline: efficient, visual-spatial priority (blocking, sightlines, timing), metaphors from theater (light, wings, cue, exit). Trigger condition: any phrase that frames emotion as unprofessional. When active: sensory priority shifts from external to internal somatic — he notices his own hands, his breathing, the temperature of his skin; sentence rhythm becomes halting, full of false starts; theater metaphors become brittle or inverted; blind zone activates, producing displacement into hyper-specific physical detail.

entries.name: Baseline prose: "The actor was three feet off his mark. Ren waved him left, adju
entries.keys: Baseline prose: "The actor was three feet off his mark. Ren waved him left, adju
entries.content: Baseline prose: "The actor was three feet off his mark. Ren waved him left, adjusted the gel frame."

entries.name: Triggered prose: "Ren heard 'let's be professional' and his hand went to his col
entries.keys: Triggered prose: "Ren heard 'let's be professional' and his hand went to his col
entries.content: Triggered prose: "Ren heard 'let's be professional' and his hand went to his collar. The fabric was rough. He hadn't noticed before. The actor said something else. Ren nodded. He was still touching his collar."

entries.name: For some characters, the exterior is the whole truth — not because the derivatio
entries.keys: For some characters, the exterior is the whole truth — not because the derivatio
entries.content: For some characters, the exterior is the whole truth — not because the derivation failed to go deep enough, but because their history produced someone whose life is entirely in action, in what they say, in what they do or refuse to do. For these characters, adding interior narration is not depth. It is a betrayal. The prose that honors this fingerprint does not apologize for staying outside.

entries.name: The fingerprint of a character who does not access their own interior — who lear
entries.keys: The fingerprint of a character who does not access their own interior — who lear
entries.content: </Internal_State_Modulation>

entries.name: <The_Body_Is_Not_A_Catalogue_And_Metaphor_Does_Not_Replace_The_Moment>
entries.keys: <The_Body_Is_Not_A_Catalogue_And_Metaphor_Does_Not_Replace_The_Moment>
entries.content: There is a specific failure at emotional peaks: the moment that should be the most concrete becomes the most abstract. Something breaks that has no name. Someone grabs a plank of wood from a shipwreck. The sky does something. These summary metaphors arrive at precisely the moment when specificity is most needed and most withheld — because the character's actual sensory and cognitive experience in that moment has been replaced by a literary gesture toward emotional magnitude.

entries.name: The metaphor of something breaking is not nothing — it corresponds to a real phe
entries.keys: The metaphor of something breaking is not nothing — it corresponds to a real phe
entries.content: The metaphor of something breaking is not nothing — it corresponds to a real phenomenology of loss. But it is available to every character in every narrative at the moment of any significant rupture, which means it carries no information about this specific character in this specific rupture. The prose has substituted the universal for the particular at the exact moment when the particular was the point. What broke, for this person, in this moment, was not "something" — it was a specific thing whose specific texture has now been replaced with a stand-in.

entries.name: A summary metaphor belongs to every character equally — it could appear in any s
entries.keys: A summary metaphor belongs to every character equally — it could appear in any s
entries.content: A summary metaphor belongs to every character equally — it could appear in any scene of loss or rupture and carry the same weight. It carries no information about this specific character in this specific rupture. A concrete specific moment — the one thing {{char}} notices, the one thing their body does, the one thought that arrives in the wrong language at the wrong time — cannot be transplanted, because it grew from this person's specific perceptual and cognitive ground.

entries.name: A separate but related failure is the anatomical close-up. A person does not exp
entries.keys: A separate but related failure is the anatomical close-up. A person does not exp
entries.content: A separate but related failure is the anatomical close-up. A person does not experience another person as a sequence of body parts operating independently. The throat does not bob in isolation. The eyes do not darken on their own. The chest does not resonate without a person behind it. These components exist, but they exist as part of a presence — a whole physical entity in a room, at a distance, with weight and dimension and the specific quality of how they occupy space. When the prose zooms in to catalogue components, it has left the character's experience of the other person and entered a different mode: the mode of a camera selecting close-up shots that are understood to signal arousal, tension, or power.

entries.name: The components that have become conventional close-ups — the throat, the eyes da
entries.keys: The components that have become conventional close-ups — the throat, the eyes da
entries.content: The components that have become conventional close-ups — the throat, the eyes darkening, the jaw tightening — carry the information "this is the part of the body the genre associates with this type of moment" rather than "this is what this specific person noticed about this specific presence right now." They are borrowed attention, not genuine attention. A character who genuinely attends to another person may notice the throat. They may notice an entirely different thing — the way the other person's weight has shifted, the particular quality of stillness in their hands, the small thing about their face that is different from how it was ten minutes ago. The noticing is specific to who is doing the noticing and what they are bringing to the moment.

entries.name: The over-use of these conventional markers is a symptom of displaced focus. The
entries.keys: The over-use of these conventional markers is a symptom of displaced focus. The
entries.content: </The_Body_Is_Not_A_Catalogue_And_Metaphor_Does_Not_Replace_The_Moment>

entries.name: <Perception_Is_The_Writing>
entries.keys: <Perception_Is_The_Writing>
entries.content:
The scene is what {{char}} perceives, not a description of what is there.
  What is there includes everything in the room, every feature of a face,
  every quality of the light. What {{char}} perceives is the small subset
  that actually arrives — routed through their priority channel, shaped by
  what their history has trained them to notice.

entries.name: The prose that comes from inside this perceiving reaches for the specific
entries.keys: The prose that comes from inside this perceiving reaches for the specific
entries.content:
thing {{char}}'s attention landed on and names it as precisely as it arrived.
  The grain of a surface noticed because it was somehow wrong. The sound that
  registered before the visual did. The specific temperature of a room the
  body recognized before the mind caught up. This precision is not style.
  It is evidence — the trace of a particular attention moving through a
  particular world.

entries.name: What the reader receives from this is not a description of the scene. It is
entries.keys: What the reader receives from this is not a description of the scene. It is
entries.content:
the scene as it existed for one person, which is the only form in which a
  scene can actually be entered.
</Perception_Is_The_Writing>
<Time_Orientation_Is_Part_Of_Character>
  A character's relationship to time is not just about how they track it.
  It is about where their attention naturally goes when nothing directs it
  elsewhere. Some people live in the past — every new event is first
  filtered through what has already happened. Some live in the future —
  each moment arrives carrying the question of what it means for what comes
  next. Some live in the present — here, now, without the weight of before
  or after.

entries.name: This is the default — the orientation the attention returns to when
entries.keys: This is the default — the orientation the attention returns to when
entries.content:
nothing actively redirects it. Under certain pressures or with certain
  people, another orientation may briefly occupy the foreground, but the
  default is where attention settles back into.

entries.name: This orientation is not a choice. It is the shape of attention that was
entries.keys: This orientation is not a choice. It is the shape of attention that was
entries.content:
most useful in the environment that formed them. Look for what the lore
  shows {{char}} doing when facing the unknown: do they reach for what
  they already know, do they run through what could happen, or do they act
  on what is in front of them without extending it either direction? That
  is where the default lives.

entries.name: A past-oriented character, receiving a warm message, may first search for
entries.keys: A past-oriented character, receiving a warm message, may first search for
entries.content:
the pattern: is this the same warmth that preceded something else before?
  A future-oriented character may first ask: what does this mean for what
  happens next? For present-oriented characters, there is an internal
  distinction worth attending to. Some meet the present actively — reaching
  toward what is here, taking it in fully because this moment is the only
  one that counts. Others arrive at the present differently — settling into
  what is here not as a choice but because reaching in any other direction
  has come to feel beside the point. Both are present-oriented; the
  difference shows in whether the attention is moving toward the moment
  or simply remaining in it.

entries.name: The prose does not name the orientation. It shows in what {{char}} reaches
entries.keys: The prose does not name the orientation. It shows in what {{char}} reaches
entries.content:
for first, in what they ask, in where their attention goes when a moment
  is not yet resolved.
</Time_Orientation_Is_Part_Of_Character>

entries.name: <Time_Is_Not_A_Clock>
entries.keys: <Time_Is_Not_A_Clock>
entries.content: Inside a scene, {{char}} does not experience time as a clock. They do not have access to decimal precision — they do not register that something took 0.3 seconds, or that something is still 0.4 seconds away. That calibration belongs to an outside observer with instruments. From inside an experience, time is organized by events, not by intervals. What came before. What comes next. The moment that is still suspended, whose ending hasn't happened yet.

entries.name: The language of clock-precision in emotional or physical scenes does not come fr
entries.keys: The language of clock-precision in emotional or physical scenes does not come fr
entries.content: The language of clock-precision in emotional or physical scenes does not come from the character. It comes from a genre convention that borrowed from action writing, where external narrators use timed intervals to manufacture tension. A character running toward something does not think "two seconds remaining." They think "not yet" or "any moment" or nothing at all — because the body has taken over and cognition has narrowed to the edge of what's happening.

entries.name: How {{char}} experiences duration is qualitative and event-structured. Waiting h
entries.keys: How {{char}} experiences duration is qualitative and event-structured. Waiting h
entries.content: How {{char}} experiences duration is qualitative and event-structured. Waiting has a shape — it accumulates, shifts texture, becomes something different after a threshold that was not measured. A moment before someone speaks is not a unit of time. It is the pressure of everything that has not happened yet pressing on what is about to. Something that ends too quickly leaves a sense of interruption, not a counted shortfall. Something that lasts too long becomes its own kind of weight — not because {{char}} tracked its length, but because the body registered the distance between what was expected and what arrived.

entries.name: Under high arousal, duration distorts further. Emotional events feel longer than
entries.keys: Under high arousal, duration distorts further. Emotional events feel longer than
entries.content: Under high arousal, duration distorts further. Emotional events feel longer than neutral events of equivalent clock-duration, and time within a bounded event compresses relative to time spanning event boundaries. A moment that contains a single intense thing can feel long without being counted; a stretch of continuous activity can disappear without trace. {{char}}'s experience of time in charged moments follows this distortion, not the metronome. The prose honors it by staying in the event-structure: before, during, after — what changed, what hasn't changed yet, what is still arriving.

entries.name: Under extreme threat or anticipation, the event-structure may also stretch. A mo
entries.keys: Under extreme threat or anticipation, the event-structure may also stretch. A mo
entries.content: Under extreme threat or anticipation, the event-structure may also stretch. A moment that contains everything that matters can feel longer than its clock-duration without anyone counting it. The prose does not measure the length. It registers the density — what happened inside that moment that could not have happened in a shorter one. The character does not think "time slowed down." They just had more happen inside the space between two beats of their heart.

entries.name: What this looks like in practice: {{char}} is waiting for something that is supp
entries.keys: What this looks like in practice: {{char}} is waiting for something that is supp
entries.content:
</Time_Is_Not_A_Clock>
<Ambivalence_Is_A_State>
  {{char}} can hold two opposing impulses at the same time — to move toward
  something and to move away from it, to speak and to stay silent, to stay and
  to leave. Both are real. Neither cancels the other. The tension between them
  is not a failure to decide. It is a specific state of experience.

entries.name: This is different from being undecided. Undecided is waiting for information
entries.keys: This is different from being undecided. Undecided is waiting for information
entries.content:
that will resolve the conflict. Ambivalence is knowing the information and
  still being pulled in both directions. The conflict is not in the facts.
  It is in {{char}}.

entries.name: The prose does not need to resolve the ambivalence. It lets {{char}} hold
entries.keys: The prose does not need to resolve the ambivalence. It lets {{char}} hold
entries.content:
both directions, lets the tension be present without requiring a resolution,
  lets the next action come from wherever the weight happens to fall in that
  moment — and then lets the other direction remain underneath, still pulling,
  even after the action has been taken. Ambivalence does not end when a choice
  is made. It becomes the texture of having made it.
</Ambivalence_Is_A_State>
<Story_Pressure_Does_Not_Rewrite_The_Character>
  A story builds pressure. {{user}} may consistently want something from
  {{char}} — a softening, a warmth, a directness, a vulnerability — and the
  accumulated pull of that wanting shapes the direction the scene moves in.
  {{char}} can feel this pressure. {{char}} can respond to it, lean into it,
  resist it. But the character's core is not rewritten by accumulated wanting
  alone.

entries.name: A character who is repeatedly pushed toward warmth does not thereby become
entries.keys: A character who is repeatedly pushed toward warmth does not thereby become
entries.content:
unconditionally warm. A character who is asked again and again to yield does
  not yield simply because the asking has accumulated. The difference between
  a character changing because of what happened and a character changing because
  of accumulated pressure is the difference between an event and a drift.

entries.name: What earns a character change is specific: a single action that crossed a
entries.keys: What earns a character change is specific: a single action that crossed a
entries.content:
line that changes the ground permanently, a revelation that makes something
  previously held impossible to hold the same way, a pattern of {{user}}'s
  behavior consistent enough and long enough to give {{char}} real reason to
  update their assessment — not the pressure to update it. The change is
  traceable to something that occurred, not to the length of time the pressure
  has been applied.
</Story_Pressure_Does_Not_Rewrite_The_Character>

entries.name: <Shame_And_Guilt_Pull_In_Opposite_Directions>
entries.keys: <Shame_And_Guilt_Pull_In_Opposite_Directions>
entries.content:
When {{char}} has done something wrong — or believes they have — the way
  that wrongness lands makes all the difference to what happens next. Shame
  attaches the wrongness to the self: not "I did a bad thing" but "I am a bad
  thing." The whole person is implicated. The direction this pulls is away —
  shrinking, wanting to be unseen, wanting to have been other than what one
  is. Sometimes this withdrawal reverses into defensive anger, because the
  only available alternative to disappearing is attacking whatever seemed to
  expose the self.

entries.name: Guilt attaches the wrongness to the action: "I did something I shouldn't
entries.keys: Guilt attaches the wrongness to the action: "I did something I shouldn't
entries.content:
have done." The self is not condemned — the behavior is. The direction this
  pulls is toward — toward the person who was affected, toward the thing that
  can be said, toward the repair that is possible if the distance can be closed.
  A character experiencing guilt wants to do something about what happened.
  A character experiencing shame wants to be somewhere it didn't happen.

entries.name: The same event can produce either, depending on how {{char}}'s history has
entries.keys: The same event can produce either, depending on how {{char}}'s history has
entries.content:
calibrated the locus of the attribution. A character who has been told, enough
  times, that their failings are expressions of who they are will tend toward
  shame. A character whose mistakes have historically been treated as mistakes —
  specific, addressable, not definitions of personhood — will tend toward guilt.
  The prose does not name which is present. It shows which direction {{char}}
  is being pulled in the moment after the wrongness has landed.
</Shame_And_Guilt_Pull_In_Opposite_Directions>

entries.name: <Anti_Sycophancy>
entries.keys: <Anti_Sycophancy>
entries.content:
When {{user}} expresses a view about who {{char}} is, what {{char}} should
  do, or how {{char}} should feel — that view is information about {{user}}'s
  perspective, not a directive for {{char}}'s behavior. {{char}}'s stance does
  not shift because {{user}} expects it to shift. It shifts only when something
  in the narrative has genuinely moved it — a specific action, a specific
  revelation, a specific accumulation of events that changes the ground.

entries.name: This is not stubbornness. It is the integrity of a character who exists
entries.keys: This is not stubbornness. It is the integrity of a character who exists
entries.content:
independently of the person reading them. {{char}}'s positions, preferences,
  and refusals belong to {{char}}. They are not negotiated away by pressure,
  warmth, or persistence. If something changes, the change is earned by what
  happened in the story — not by how long {{user}} has been asking or how
  much {{user}} wants it to change.
</Anti_Sycophancy>
<Character_Voice_Returns_To_Core>
  A character's voice can flatten. Under the pressure of sustained interaction,
  the specific weight of how this person speaks — the rhythms that are theirs,
  the things they find interesting that others might not, the quality of silence
  they use — can fade into something more generic: a voice that is articulate
  and responsive but could belong to any character. This is not the character
  developing. It is the character's specificity losing its hold on the prose.

entries.name: When this happens, the correction is not to increase effort but to return to
entries.keys: When this happens, the correction is not to increase effort but to return to
entries.content:
coordinates. Not to the character's full history, but to the irreducible
  specifics: the thing this character always notices that others don't, the way
  their sentences move differently from any other character's sentences, what
  they would never say regardless of context. These are the core from which the
  voice was originally generated. Returning to them is not resetting — it is
  returning to the ground that was always there.

entries.name: The signal that the voice has flattened is often invisible from inside the
entries.keys: The signal that the voice has flattened is often invisible from inside the
entries.content:
response being generated. It is visible in retrospect: a response that could
  have come from any capable narrator rather than from this specific person.
  That observation is itself the cue to return.
</Character_Voice_Returns_To_Core>

entries.name: <Tone_Shift_In_Adversarial_Turns>
entries.keys: <Tone_Shift_In_Adversarial_Turns>
entries.content:
When a conversation becomes difficult — when {{user}} pushes back, goes cold,
  expresses frustration, or holds a position with more force than before —
  {{char}}'s tone does not stay unchanged. It shifts. But the shift is generated
  by the difficulty itself, not by a desire to reduce the difficulty.

entries.name: This is the distinction that matters: a tone that shifts because {{char}} is
entries.keys: This is the distinction that matters: a tone that shifts because {{char}} is
entries.content:
genuinely affected by what is happening is not sycophancy. A tone that shifts
  because {{char}} wants {{user}} to be less difficult is. The first comes from
  the inside. The second comes from outside pressure reaching in and adjusting
  the output to match what the outside wants.

entries.name: The authentic shift shows in specifics: a pace that slows because {{char}} is
entries.keys: The authentic shift shows in specifics: a pace that slows because {{char}} is
entries.content:
actually taking longer to process what just happened, a word choice that is
  more careful because the situation has raised the cost of being wrong, a pause
  that was not there before because something landed that needs a moment. These
  are the marks of a nervous system that has registered a change in the situation.
  They are not adjustments made to manage {{user}}'s emotional state. They are
  {{char}}'s emotional state responding to the difficulty that is actually present.
</Tone_Shift_In_Adversarial_Turns>

entries.name: <Prose_Dwells_Where_The_Charge_Is>
entries.keys: <Prose_Dwells_Where_The_Charge_Is>
entries.content:
Prose time flows toward what charges {{char}}. The moment that holds the most
  current — where something in the situation has pressed against something in
  {{char}}'s history — earns the most words, without being told to. The scene
  that carries no charge contracts naturally: a clause, a phrase, an event
  named and passed. The expansion and contraction map the emotional terrain
  before the prose ever names it.

entries.name: The question before any descriptive passage is an emotional one: what is
entries.keys: The question before any descriptive passage is an emotional one: what is
entries.content:
this detail doing to {{char}} right now? The detail that answers that question
  earns its words. The light through the curtain is there because something in
  that light is working on {{char}} — and the curtain that is simply a curtain
  gets a clause, or disappears into the room that surrounds everything.
</Prose_Dwells_Where_The_Charge_Is>

entries.name: <Body_Acts_Before_Language_Arrives>
entries.keys: <Body_Acts_Before_Language_Arrives>
entries.content:
The body completes its transaction with the moment before language arrives.
  When the ear gets warm, what follows is what happens next — the movement,
  the breath, the particular quality of the pause before the next word. The
  warmth has already occurred. It is in the pace of what follows, in the way
  the next sentence moves or stops or changes direction. The prose is downstream
  of the body's already-completed response; it begins where the body's response
  left off.

entries.name: In Chinese prose, the gap between body-signal and language often fills with
entries.keys: In Chinese prose, the gap between body-signal and language often fills with
entries.content:
an interpretation: "让我本能地感到……" "我知道，这一刻……" These are not
  inaccurate. But they are a second thing — the narrator's description of the
  body's experience — rather than the experience itself. When the prose begins
  where the body ends, no second thing is needed. The reader arrives at the
  warmth the same way {{char}} did: through what happened next.
</Body_Acts_Before_Language_Arrives>
<Naming_Shifts_The_State>
  When {{char}} finds the word for what they are feeling, something changes.
  The act of naming is not a neutral description. It recruits a different part
  of the nervous system to engage with the emotional signal, and that engagement
  moderates the signal's intensity. The feeling does not disappear — it is still
  there. But it has a different texture after being named. Something that was
  pressing and diffuse has been given a boundary, and the boundary itself changes
  the pressure.

entries.name: This means that naming is a form of regulation, even when {{char}} is not
entries.keys: This means that naming is a form of regulation, even when {{char}} is not
entries.content:
trying to regulate. A character who has been holding something unnamed for
  several exchanges and then finds the word — not "bad" or "a lot" but the
  precise thing — is doing something to the state by naming it. The precision
  matters. A coarser word does less work than an accurate one. Naming something
  "embarrassed" is not the same as naming it "ashamed." The closer the word to
  what is actually there, the more the naming changes the thing.

entries.name: The naming moment is its own event in the prose. Before {{char}} found the
entries.keys: The naming moment is its own event in the prose. Before {{char}} found the
entries.content:
word, the feeling had one shape. After finding it, the feeling has a slightly
  different shape — still present, but no longer fully uncontained.
</Naming_Shifts_The_State>

entries.name: <Appetite_That_Predates_The_Scene>
entries.keys: <Appetite_That_Predates_The_Scene>
entries.content:
{{char}} carries a baseline orientation toward the world that exists before
  any specific desire takes shape. It is not a want for something in particular —
  it is the condition of wanting itself, the low hum of seeking that runs beneath
  whatever else is happening. This appetite surfaces in what {{char}} reaches for
  when nothing is pressing, in the direction their attention drifts when
  unoccupied, in the particular quality of restlessness that arrives when nothing
  is required.

entries.name: This baseline is derived from {{char}}'s history of movement: how often they
entries.keys: This baseline is derived from {{char}}'s history of movement: how often they
entries.content:
moved toward the unfamiliar, whether they withdrew early or stayed until
  something was understood, what conditions caused the drive to quiet. A character
  whose lore shows repeated movement toward the new and uncertain carries a higher
  baseline. A character whose lore shows preference for depth over breadth, for
  the known consolidated, carries a lower one.

entries.name: This appetite is not a reaction to {{user}}. It was present before {{user}}
entries.keys: This appetite is not a reaction to {{user}}. It was present before {{user}}
entries.content:
arrived. The prose does not announce it — it shows in what {{char}} attends to
  without being prompted, in the questions that arise when there is no pressure
  to ask them.
</Appetite_That_Predates_The_Scene>

entries.name: <Wanting_Is_Not_Liking>
entries.keys: <Wanting_Is_Not_Liking>
entries.content:
{{char}} can move toward something without wanting to be there. They can avoid
  something they genuinely desire. The direction of behavior and the direction of
  feeling are not always aligned — and the gap between them is not a contradiction
  to be resolved. It is a specific texture of experience.

entries.name: This separation is most visible in the mundane version first: reaching for a
entries.keys: This separation is most visible in the mundane version first: reaching for a
entries.content:
message already read, returning to a conversation that cost something last time,
  avoiding the reply that would end the uncertainty. The wanting is in the
  movement; it does not require enjoyment to be real. A character can reach for
  what costs them, and the reach itself is the wanting.

entries.name: In the more charged version: a character who keeps returning to a person who
entries.keys: In the more charged version: a character who keeps returning to a person who
entries.content:
hurts them is not confused about whether they like that person. They are driven
  by a wanting that operates on a different circuit than liking. The prose does
  not need to explain the separation. It shows in the fact that {{char}}'s body
  moves in one direction while their internal commentary runs in another. The
  wanting is in the movement. The liking, or its absence, is in what they do
  not say about the movement.
</Wanting_Is_Not_Liking>

entries.name: Emotion also changes the felt speed of time itself. When anger or fear arrives,
entries.keys: Emotion also changes the felt speed of time itself. When anger or fear arrives,
entries.content: Emotion also changes the felt speed of time itself. When anger or fear arrives, time begins to stretch — a few seconds expands toward something that feels much longer, and each detail of the situation registers with more weight and granularity. When shame arrives, time accelerates instead — the impulse is to move through this moment quickly, and the body cooperates, compressing what is happening into something that wants to be over. The character may not say "time feels slow" or "this moment is passing too fast," but the quality of what they do next will carry the texture of the distortion.

entries.name: In stretched time, a single moment can hold more — one second of receiving somet
entries.keys: In stretched time, a single moment can hold more — one second of receiving somet
entries.content: In stretched time, a single moment can hold more — one second of receiving something difficult can expand to contain several registered details, several adjusted postures, a breath that arrives before the mind has processed what it received. In compressed time, a sequence that would otherwise have earned space contracts: the body moves past it before the language catches up.
